### 2026-10-06 – # Hack Life Journal

**1.5h**

# Hack Life Journal

## October 5th

Today I figured out how to set up an **SSD1306 OLED display**, using a website called **Wokwi**. Wokwi provides virtual components that simulate how they would work in real life, before using actual hardware. You can even code Arduino code on it that functions with the electronic tools.

###  OLED Display Setup
![Screenshot 2026-10-05 at 5.38.45 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/gkojKygsM9FRIeDe3FDErW56Isuc9VSK/e667e6eea4e40925b562b0b3509f210affd0f0d8b1e4ed630d6562774e99d327.png)

###  What I Learned
- How to connect and configure an **SSD1306 OLED display**.
- How to use **Wokwi** to simulate electronic circuits
- Display custom text on the OLED screen.
- Create scrolling text effect

### Struggles & Lessons Learned
-  **Arduino Mega**, the **SDA** pin always connects to **Digital Pin 20**.
- **SCL** pin always connects to **Digital Pin 21**.
- Couldn't find an **Arduino Mega 2560** in KiCad

I was so confused because when I researched the Oled Display for Arduinos, it said that SDA goes to A5 and that SCL to A4. I did so more research and found out that SCL and SDA goes to different pins depending on the microcontroller. Since KiCad doesn't have the mega 2560, I made a practice schematic of my design of the display, which I put in my Lapse.
### Plans For Tomorrow
-  Build Practice PCBS by watching youtube
- Learn to use Temp/Humidity Sensor
- Figure out how to use parts that aren't built in KiCad

### 2026-10-07 – # Hack Life Journal

**2.2h**

# Hack Life Journal

## Tuesday, October 6th

Today, I finalized my wiring diagram and connected the OLED display and DHT22 temperature/humidity sensor so the OLED could display live temperature readings.

Sadly, I wasn't able to learn how to create custom PCB frame designs like I had planned because I had a lot of AP homework to finish.

### Final Wiring + Coded Features:

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 7.30.11 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/gkojKygsM9FRIeDe3FDErW56Isuc9VSK/505c918d824d8d57d2acd444ea6615843e844df225f3921d88a745b3b5902887.png)

## Design Decisions & Learning

- I improved my design after realizing that the Arduino Uno R3 was too large for a clean PCB layout. I switched to an Arduino Nano, which made the design much more compact.

- I converted the temperature readings from Celsius to Fahrenheit so the display would be easier for me to read.

- I learned that the NC (No Connection) pin on the DHT22 does not have any internal function, which is why it is not connected to anything in my schematic.

- I learned how the F( ); function works which  tells the Arduino Nano to  save info on the flash memory, which is a kind of storage that retains data much longer, despite the device being off. This saves space in the RAM, or random accessed memory which is super fast at processing but can't carry as much data compared to flash memory. This functions keep   the RAM storage from being taken up, while still processing data and task swiftly.

- I learned how to add the serial monitor to Wokwi, since it doesn't have it built in. Here is the image of the JSON that I edited to implement the serial monitor. If you look to the bottom right of the image, you can see the serial monitor works!!!!

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 7.53.46 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/gkojKygsM9FRIeDe3FDErW56Isuc9VSK/308b5d7c5db933116ae5627e6708da78b8cfa1749b9c0b99464524eb02747721.png)

The line of code that made it work was:

 "serialMonitor": {"display": "always", "newline": "lf"}

## Plans for Tomorrow

- Add the logic required to make the bar LEDs work.
- Continue refining the PCB design.
- Start learning how to create custom PCB shapes and board outlines.
